research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 14368 (signed 2025-12-18; 90 FR 60521; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14368.txt, read in full) sets the 2026 rates of basic pay for the statutory pay systems, the Senior Executive Service, the Executive Schedule, the Vice President, the Congress, judges, the uniformed services and administrative law judges, sets locality payments, and supersedes Executive Order 14132. Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 14368 of December 18, 2025, on adjustments of certain rates of pay at 90 FR 60521, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory fragments the sections and contains a fragment that is only a schedule numeral, so I replaced it with nine clauses (inventory override): the authority recital and sections 1 to 8. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; section 7 fixes when the schedules take effect and section 8 supersedes EO 14132 as of those dates, and neither is recorded as an end because the exact dates for every applicable pay period are not held in a packet source. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 14368 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy, the Federal Register contents page of December 23, 2025 and OPM's notice of February 3, 2026 that implements it; no held text revokes, supersedes or amends it, and a later annual pay order would postdate the checked period for rates effective in January 2027. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 1, 1 and 0 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the held OPM notice that publishes the section 5(b) notice is not a packet source, so I do not claim that the Federal Register publication duty ended, and sections 4 and 5(b) are carried as continuing for that reason.

The order itself supersedes EO 14132 (section 8), an earlier order's end that is not an end of this order.","independent_command_check":"The statutory pay schedules (section 1), the Senior Executive Service ranges (section 2), the Executive, legislative and judicial salaries (section 3), the uniformed services rates and the law enforcement pay assessment (section 4), locality payments and their implementation (section 5), administrative law judge rates (section 6), the effective-date rule (section 7) and the supersession of EO 14132 (section 8) are separate; none was found ended.","savings_check":"The order has no savings or transition clause; the supersession of EO 14132 in section 8 is the order's own act and not a savings clause, so no savings source other than the order itself is needed.","scope_check":"The corrected inventory has nine clauses covering the whole order: the authority recital and sections 1 to 8."}

savings.reason: EO 14368 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause; section 8's supersession of EO 14132 operates as of the section 7 dates and no held instrument ends the schedules, so no residual effect is claimed apart from the continuing clauses.
